reporting.what: When this is on, anyone who has the link, or who scans the QR code of a unit, can send a report without signing in: a visitor, a member of the public, or a member of staff with no account. These reports are always anonymous. They arrive in the incidents list like any other, and the sender gets a follow-up code to read your replies.

deadlines.title: Deadlines for triage and closure
deadlines.what: These numbers set how long your organization allows itself to triage a new report and to close an incident, by harm level. Both are counted from the moment the report is made. Anything past its time shows as overdue in the incidents list and on the dashboard, and the people responsible for it are notified.
deadlines.applies: A change applies to new reports, and to an incident whose harm level or sentinel flag is changed afterwards: its closure deadline is then worked out again from this table. Other deadlines already set do not move. Hours and days are calendar time, so nights, weekends and holidays count.

rules: One document per row in a CSV file, or per object in a JSON file. Save the file as UTF-8 text.
CSV: the first row names the columns. Fields are separated by commas or by semicolons; a field holding a separator, quotation marks or line breaks is written between double quotation marks.

JSON: a list of documents, or an object whose “documents” holds the list. A text per language is an object keyed by language code; section texts sit under “sections”, by section key, then by language.
Dates are written as year-month-day, for example 2024-03-01.
Several values in one column are separated by |, for example ICU|ER.
“acknowledge” is yes or no; “confidentiality” is all_staff or restricted.

A number left empty is given by Trustline. A number given is kept as written on the original, in letters (Latin, or those of your organization's languages) and digits, with spaces, hyphens, full stops, slashes, underscores or brackets between them, at most 40 characters, and must not already be used.

Tables and figures cannot be imported as such. Write a table as a list, one line per row; for a figure or a flowchart, say so in “differences”, for example “Appendix B flowchart not reproduced, see the original”.

request.responsibility: Once the file is downloaded, your organization is responsible for it as the controller of that data: keep it where only those who need it can open it, and delete it when it is no longer needed.
request.onlyOne: An export is already under way. Only one can be asked for at a time.
request.noteHelp: Optional. Seen by the person who approves.
request.languageHelp: The READMEs, file headings and document pages are in this language.
request.passwordHelp: Asking is signed with your password.

list.title: Exports
list.empty: No export has been asked for yet.
list.lapses: Lapses on {time} if no one approves it.
list.failed: It could not be made. Trustline has been told; ask for it again later.
list.ready: Ready: {size}. It can be downloaded until {expires}, {left} more times.

approve.intro: Approving lets the archive be made. Sign with your password.
approve.done: Approved. The archive is being made.

refuse.reasonHelp: Required. The person who asked sees it.

download.intro: Downloading is signed with your password, and recorded in the audit trail.
download.done: Downloaded. Check its fingerprint against the one shown here.

check.title: How to check an archive
check.fingerprint: 1. Its SHA-256 fingerprint must match the one shown with the export. On most computers:
check.manifest: 2. Inside, manifest.sig is Trustline's signature of manifest.json. Check it with Trustline's published export key, never with a key found in the archive.
check.files: 3. manifest.json lists every file with its fingerprint; the README in the archive says how to check each one.

errors.wrong_password: That password is not right. Nothing was done. Type it again.
errors.password_locked: Too many wrong passwords: your account is locked for 15 minutes. Nothing was done.
errors.language_mismatch: Choose one of the organization's languages.
errors.export_in_progress: An export is already under way. Wait until it is done, refused or cancelled.
errors.same_person: You asked for this export, so someone else must approve or refuse it.
errors.lapsed: This request lapsed without approval. Ask for a new export.
errors.stale_export: This export changed in the meantime. It is shown as it is now: check it, then try again.
errors.not_requester: Only the person who asked can cancel this request.
errors.not_yours: You may not download this export.
errors.not_ready: This export is not ready yet. Wait until it is.
errors.download_limit: This export has been downloaded as many times as allowed. Ask for a new export if you need it again.
errors.expired: This export has expired and was deleted. Ask for a new export.
errors.notFound: This export no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.invalid: Check the fields: something is missing or too long.
errors.generic: Could not do this. Try again.
